title: Review: Cell theory, microscopes and magnification; Protein secretion and the endomembrane system; Cell specialisation, tissues, organs; Prokaryotic cells and viruses
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE07a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE03#t2 term and clue written for the game; CE01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE07b#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE01a#N.12, CE01b#N.5, CE04a#N.9, CE07a#N.10b, CE01a#N.9, CE01b#N.2, CE04a#N.13a, CE07a#N.3a, CE01a#N.6, CE01b#N.12, CE04a#N.3a, CE07a#N.11. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Zygote
items.clue: The single cell from which a whole body is built up by mitosis

items.label: Glycoproteins
items.clue: Molecules made when carbohydrate chains are added to polypeptides

items.label: Magnification
items.clue: Image size divided by actual size; written with no unit, e.g. ×2000

items.label: Guard cells
items.clue: A pair around each stoma that swell with water and bend apart to open it

questions.stem: A micrograph shows a pollen grain 60 mm across. A scale bar on the micrograph is 20 mm long and is labelled 10 µm. What is the actual diameter of the pollen grain?

options.text: 3 µm
30 µm
60 µm
120 µm

questions.explanation: Magnification = 20 000 µm ÷ 10 µm = ×2000. Actual size = 60 000 µm ÷ 2000 = 30 µm.

questions.stem: A student wants to watch living white blood cells engulfing bacteria about 2 µm long. Which choice of microscope, with its reason, is correct?

options.text: A TEM, as its high resolution would show each step of the engulfing in detail.
An SEM, as its 3D image of the surface would show the cell membrane moving live.
A light microscope, as the cells stay alive and 2 µm is well above its limit.
A light microscope, as extra stain would make the small bacteria appear sharper.

questions.explanation: Living cells can be watched, and bacteria 2 µm long are about ten times larger than the 200 nm resolution limit, so they are clearly resolved.

questions.stem: A bacterial cell contains one circular DNA molecule and six copies of a plasmid. It divides once by binary fission. Which statement about the two daughter cells is correct?

options.text: Each has one circular DNA molecule, wound around histones, and exactly three plasmids.
Each has one copy of the circular DNA; the number of plasmids in each can differ.
Each has half of the original circular DNA molecule and three of the plasmids.
Each has its circular DNA inside a new nucleus formed after the chromosomes separate.

questions.explanation: The circular DNA is replicated once, so each daughter receives one copy. Plasmids are replicated and distributed independently, so their number varies between daughter cells.

questions.stem: The wall of the stomach contains epithelium, smooth muscle and connective tissue. Together they digest and churn food. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Epithelium, muscle and connective tissue are each organs, as each has a function.
The stomach is an organ system, as it contains several different tissues.
The stomach is an organ: several tissues working together for an overall function.
Epithelium is not a tissue if it contains goblet cells as well as other cells.

questions.explanation: Epithelium, muscle and connective tissue each do one job; together they perform digestion, the stomach's overall function.

questions.stem: With the ×40 objective lens in place, 40 divisions of an eyepiece graticule line up exactly with 100 µm on a stage micrometer. Using the same objective, a cell spans 44 graticule divisions. What is the actual length of the cell in millimetres?

options.text: 1.1 mm

questions.explanation: 100 µm ÷ 40 = 2.5 µm per division with this objective. 44 × 2.5 µm = 110 µm = 0.11 mm.

questions.stem: Ribosomes are about 25 nm across. They cannot be seen with a light microscope but are clearly visible in electron micrographs. What is the reason?

options.text: Electrons have a far shorter wavelength than light, so the resolution is much higher.
The electron microscope magnifies many more times, so much smaller objects become visible.
Heavy-metal stains used for electron microscopy make small structures much sharper.
Electron microscopes use fluorescent stains that make ribosomes glow in the dark.

questions.explanation: Light limits a light microscope to about 200 nm, so a 25 nm ribosome cannot be resolved; the electron beam's much shorter wavelength gives resolution below 1 nm.

questions.stem: An electron micrograph shows a cell about 3 µm long. It has a cell wall, a paler fibrous region of DNA not enclosed by any membrane, many small dense granules, and no membrane-bound organelles. How should the cell be classified?

options.text: As a plant cell, because a cell wall is found only around the cells of plants.
As a eukaryote, because the region containing DNA must be a nucleus, as every cell has one.
As a prokaryote, because its DNA lies in a nucleoid region and it has no membrane-bound organelles.
As a eukaryote, because prokaryotic cells are too simple to contain any ribosomes.

questions.stem: In a human, a neuron and a liver cell are both descended by mitosis from the same zygote. What is the difference between them once they have differentiated?

options.text: They express different subsets of the same complete set of genes.
They have kept different sets of genes and discarded the rest.
They were set on different paths inside from fertilisation.
They differ only until the body needs to swap them over.

questions.explanation: All cells produced by mitosis from the zygote inherit the full genome. The neuron switches on the genes for its proteins and the liver cell a different set, while both keep every gene.

questions.stem: In a photomicrograph taken at a magnification of ×2000, a red blood cell measures 15 mm across. What is the actual width of the cell?

options.text: 7.5 µm

questions.explanation: Actual size = 15 mm ÷ 2000 = 0.0075 mm, which is 7.5 µm (1 mm = 1000 µm): the typical diameter of a red blood cell.

questions.stem: A virus particle is about 100 nm across. A student photographs a stained sample through a light microscope at ×1500, then enlarges the photo 20 times: a total magnification of ×30 000. At this magnification a 100 nm particle would be 3 mm across. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: Its shape will be visible, as anything 3 mm across in a photo can be seen by eye.
Its shape will be visible if more stain is added to make the image sharper.
Its shape will be visible with a higher-power objective instead of enlarging the photo.
No shape will be seen: the particle is below the 200 nm limit, so enlarging only enlarges blur.

questions.stem: Which description of the structure of a Bacillus cell is correct?

options.text: A loop of naked DNA lies in the cytoplasm, and proteins are made on 70S ribosomes.
The DNA is enclosed by a nuclear membrane inside a small nucleus within the cytoplasm.
The cell wall outside the plasma membrane is built from long parallel fibres of cellulose.
The DNA loop is wound around histone proteins to package it within the nucleoid region.

questions.explanation: A Gram-positive eubacterium such as Bacillus has a cell wall, a plasma membrane, cytoplasm, naked DNA in a loop lying in the nucleoid region of the cytoplasm, and 70S ribosomes on which its proteins are synthesised.

questions.stem: In a hypothetical species of plant, leaf cells make large amounts of a protein that binds chlorophyll, but the root cells of the same plant make none of it. Which statement best explains this difference?

options.text: In root cells, the base sequence of the gene has been changed, and the gene no longer codes for the protein.
Both cell types carry the gene for the protein, but it is expressed in leaf cells and not in root cells.
Root cells have lost the gene for the protein from their DNA because they did not use it.
Root cells do not need the protein, so they choose not to make it, unlike the cells of leaves.
